steps.title: Суффикс -able
steps.html:
-able после глагола значит это можно с ним сделать: wash → washable, replace → replaceable.

un- в начале меняет знак: unemployable, unwashable, irreplaceable (здесь ir-, а не un-).

Глагол на немую -e обычно сохраняет её перед -able, если нужно мягкое c или g: replace → replaceable, manage → manageable.

steps.title: Два способа добавить информацию
steps.html:
Cars which drive themselves have been on the roads for years. — придаточное говорит, какие именно машины. Убрать нельзя.

The driver, who is sitting in heavy traffic, presses a button. — мы уже знаем, какой водитель. Это добавление, оно в запятых.

…the people whose skills are easier to copy… — whose показывает принадлежность.

steps.title: В каком предложении нужны запятые?
options: Cars which drive themselves are already legal in California.
My car which is fifteen years old still passes its test.
People who have high-level skills will still have work.
steps.answer: My car which is fifteen years old still passes its test.
steps.why: Машина одна, поэтому придаточное — дополнительная информация: My car, which is fifteen years old, still passes its test.

Можно ли опустить местоимение?да, если это дополнение: the car (that) I boughtнет, никогда
ПримерPeople who have no skills risk being unemployable.Rolls-Royce, which is British, has described robo-ships.

steps.title: Как это работает
steps.html:
Проверка: уберите придаточное. Если смысл указывает на то же самое — оно было дополнительным, ставьте запятые.

В определяющем можно опустить who/which/that, если это дополнение: the car (that) I bought. Нельзя, если это подлежащее: the car that broke down.

which может относиться к целой мысли, в добавляющем: It can talk to the cars around it, which is why it can overtake safely.

where и when работают так же для мест и времени: the junction where it happened.

90% of these accidents are caused by human error, which is the strongest argument for the technology.

steps.title: The car that drives itself
steps.html:
Прочитайте один раз. Автор даёт обе стороны — найдите их.

The driver, who is sitting in heavy traffic on the motorway, presses a button on the steering wheel and takes his hands off it. The car is now driving. This is not a demonstration: cars which drive themselves have been on the roads in California for several years.

Most of it is already in the car you own. Cars that park themselves, brake automatically when the vehicle in front slows down, and warn you when you are slipping out of your lane are ordinary equipment now. A driverless car, which simply joins those systems together and adds fast broadband, is the next step rather than a new idea. Because it can talk to the cars around it, it can overtake safely and drive at speed much closer to them, which is why some engineers believe the traffic jam is a problem we have already solved.

The argument for it is a number. More than fifty million people are killed or injured on the roads every year, and around ninety per cent of those accidents are caused by human error. A computer that sticks to the speed limit does not get tired, does not look at its phone, and does not decide that this junction is worth the risk.

The argument against it is also a number, and it is about work. Machines which can serve customers, give directions and drive a lorry are becoming part of everyone's life, and the people whose skills are easier to copy than a machine's are the ones who lose. Amazon has promised delivery drones; Rolls-Royce has described robo-ships that will need no crew at all.

So the question has changed. It is no longer whether the technology works — for the most part it already does. It is what we owe the driver, whose job we are about to automate, and who has been doing it perfectly well for thirty years.

The car that drives itself

The driver, who is sitting in heavy traffic on the motorway, presses a button on the steering wheel and takes his hands off it. The car is now driving. This is not a demonstration: cars which drive themselves have been on the roads in California for several years.

Most of it is already in the car you own. Cars that park themselves, brake automatically when the vehicle in front slows down, and warn you when you are slipping out of your lane are ordinary equipment now. A driverless car, which simply joins those systems together and adds fast broadband, is the next step rather than a new idea. Because it can talk to the cars around it, it can overtake safely and drive at speed much closer to them, which is why some engineers believe the traffic jam is a problem we have already solved.

The argument for it is a number. More than fifty million people are killed or injured on the roads every year, and around ninety per cent of those accidents are caused by human error. steps.title: Ответьте вслух.
items: Сели бы вы в машину без водителя? Объясните, используя придаточное.
Какую работу в вашем городе машина заберёт первой? Опишите тех, чья это работа.
Назовите навык, который машина не скопирует, и объясните почему.

steps.title: Теперь ответьте одним высказыванием. Запишите себя.
steps.sub: Используйте минимум одно определяющее и одно добавляющее придаточное.
items: The machine that has changed my day most is … .
My phone, which … , now does things that … .
The people whose jobs will go first are … , which is why … .

steps.title: Урок 16 пройден
items: Я добавляю информацию через who, which, that и whose.
Я различаю определяющее и добавляющее придаточное и ставлю запятые.
Я могу говорить о машинах и навыках, которые они заменяют.
Я по-прежнему выбираю между Present Perfect и Past Simple.
